card.name: Semba
card.era: Rose to popularity in the 1950s; older roots
card.tagline: Angola's playful partner dance, ancestor of samba and kizomba
card.profile: Semba is a traditional Angolan music and social partner dance that rose in popularity in the 1950s with the development of modern Angolan music led by the group Ngola Ritmos (Kizomba/Wikipedia; Music of Angola). The name derives from the Kimbundu "massemba," referring to the umbigada — a move in which the man pulls his partner close until their bellies touch. It is a lively, fast-footed couple dance full of improvisation and showmanship, danced for entertainment at parties rather than as ritual.
card.insight: Semba is widely cited as the direct predecessor of several major styles — Brazilian samba, kizomba and kuduro — making it a foundational pillar of Angolan musical identity and a living link between Africa and the wider Lusophone and Latin American worlds (Music of Angola).
